description: JVM backend skeleton conformance (ISSUE-0091). Fixtures for the JVM backend (several also run under LuaJIT as the reference behavior): literals/output, int arithmetic, local variables, if/else, a frontend compile-error rejected before the backend, and the observable-behavior regressions: null-typed returns/initializers with side effects, null-typed captures of reassigned locals and parameters, floored % on negative operands, string equality/ordering (Unicode scalar-value order), console.error -> stderr, null equality, standalone expression statements, module-level load-time statements, a module-load-only fixture (runner initializes the module class when no function is auto-invoked), non-finite number literals (1e999 -> Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY), && / || short-circuit preservation for guarded null-typed calls, and a module-level error with a zero-arity export (the runner unwraps ExceptionInInitializerError into the DEAL_ERROR_CODE contract). The JVM adapter compiles the emitted Java artifact with javac and executes it with java in a subprocess; the generated runner auto-invokes zero-arity exported functions in declaration order and prints their non-null results, so expectedOutput observes real return values (console.log output is also captured). The Lua harness auto-invokes in pairs() (unspecified) order, so fixtures with multiple zero-arity exports must not depend on cross-backend invocation order (every fixture here has at most one zero-arity export).

tests.name: jvm-literals-output
tests.description: Literals of every primitive kind flow through functions and locals, and std/console output reaches stdout

tests.name: jvm-int-arithmetic
tests.description: Checked int arithmetic (+ - * / % **) computes 41 through a call chain

tests.name: jvm-local-variable
tests.description: Local variables, reassignment, and inner-block shadowing compute 111

tests.name: jvm-if-else
tests.description: if/else-if/else branches and unary negation classify negative, zero, and positive values

tests.name: jvm-frontend-error-rejected
tests.description: A type error is rejected by the frontend before any backend runs (codegen/javac/java never invoked)
tests.source: let a: int = 1.0;

tests.name: jvm-null-return-log
tests.description: A null-typed return expression that is a console.log call keeps its observable side effect (LuaJIT prints 'x' before returning; the expression must not be discarded)
tests.source:
import * as console from "std/console"
export function test(): null { return console.log("x"); }

tests.name: jvm-null-return-helper
tests.description: A null-typed return expression that is a direct null-returning call keeps its observable side effect (LuaJIT prints 'helper-ran' before returning)

tests.name: jvm-null-var-init
tests.description: Initializing a null-typed local from a void-returning call evaluates the call and stores null (LuaJIT prints 'assign-log' at the let)

tests.name: jvm-module-level-statements
tests.description: Module-level statements (console.log and an if) run at load time, in source order relative to field initializers — LuaJIT executes them at require time

tests.name: jvm-module-level-assignment
tests.description: A module-level assignment to a module field is visible to exported functions (LuaJIT executes it at load time)

tests.name: jvm-shadowed-initializer
tests.description: A shadowed let whose initializer references its own name binds the RHS to the OUTER binding (LuaJIT's `local x = x + 1` reads the outer x, computing 6)

tests.name: jvm-null-capture-reassigned
tests.description: A null-typed initializer that captures a local reassigned after the capture compiles and runs (a lambda lowering would make javac reject the artifact: local variables referenced from a lambda must be effectively final)

tests.name: jvm-null-capture-parameter
tests.description: A null-typed initializer that captures a parameter reassigned after the capture compiles and runs

tests.name: jvm-null-arg-capture
tests.description: A null-typed call argument that captures a local reassigned after the capture compiles and runs

tests.name: jvm-nummod-negative
tests.description: number % is Lua-style floored modulo on negative operands: -7.0 % 3.0 == 2.0 (Java's truncated % would give -1.0)
tests.source: export function test(): number { return -7.0 % 3.0; }

tests.name: jvm-string-eq-order
tests.description: String ===/!== and ordering compare by content end to end: classify returns 1 for equal, 2 for less-than, 3 otherwise

tests.name: jvm-console-error
tests.description: console.error writes to stderr (captured by the runner's merged stream)
tests.source:
import * as console from "std/console"
export function test(): null { console.error("err-chan"); }

tests.name: jvm-null-equality
tests.description: null === null is true and null !== null is false (spec §Value equality); z === null emits Java ==

tests.name: jvm-standalone-expression
tests.description: A standalone non-call expression statement (x + 1;) is genuinely evaluated like LuaJIT evaluates it (lowered to a dummy local), not rejected or discarded

tests.name: jvm-standalone-expression-overflow
tests.description: A standalone expression statement that overflows reports E8004 — evaluation is real, matching LuaJIT

tests.name: jvm-module-load-only
tests.description: A module with no zero-arity exported functions still runs its module-level statements: the runner initializes the module class so the static initializers execute

tests.name: jvm-module-load-error
tests.description: A module-level runtime error in a module with no zero-arity exported functions still reports the DEAL error code: the runner initializes the module class and unwraps the initialization error
tests.source:
let x: int = 1 / 0;
export function takesArg(y: int): int { return y; }

tests.name: jvm-nonfinite-literal
tests.description: A number literal that overflows to infinity (1e999, checker-accepted: the parser stores Double.parseDouble with no range check) emits the Double constant instead of a bare Infinity identifier that javac rejects — the CLI must never report success for an artifact javac rejects; LuaJIT emits (1/0) for the same literal
tests.source: export function test(): number { let x: number = 1e999; return x; }

tests.name: jvm-nonfinite-negated
tests.description: Negating an overflowing number literal (-1e999) prints -Infinity; LuaJIT emits (-1/0) for the same literal
tests.source: export function test(): number { let x: number = -1e999; return x; }

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-and
tests.description: The right operand of && is NOT evaluated when the left operand is false (LuaJIT's `and` short-circuit): a null-typed side-effecting call in the guarded operand must not run — if it ran, counter would become 1 and the program would print 'ran'. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-or
tests.description: The right operand of || is NOT evaluated when the left operand is true: the guarded null-typed call must not run (b stays true, counter stays 0, prints 'skipped'). Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-shortcircuit-runs
tests.description: A guarded operand that IS reachable still evaluates: true && helper() === null runs helper() (the guard must not swallow reachable side effects)

tests.name: jvm-string-scalar-order
tests.description: String ordering compares Unicode scalar values (LuaJIT orders bytewise in UTF-8, which is scalar order): U+1F600 < U+E000 is FALSE in scalar order, though UTF-16 code-unit order (String.compareTo) says true — a compareTo lowering would print 'utf16'. Runs under both backends; LuaJIT is the reference behavior

tests.name: jvm-module-error-with-export
tests.description: A module-level runtime error in a module WITH a zero-arity exported function still reports the DEAL error code: the first auto-invocation triggers class initialization, whose ExceptionInInitializerError (a LinkageError, not a RuntimeException) wraps the DealError — the runner unwraps it into the DEAL_ERROR_CODE contract
tests.source:
export function test(): int { return 1; }
let x: int = 1 / 0;
